query: Earlier empirical-potential and first-principles studies primarily targeted phase-transition temperature, while other fusion properties remain difficult because they require free energies on both sides of the transition with vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling retained. Explicit ab initio free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but depends on costly molecular dynamics. TOR-TILD increased throughput for elemental and binary systems, yet slows substantially for multicomponent high-entropy systems. Under the constraint that the free energies of both solid and fluid states and the relevant entropy terms remain faithful, what single testable methodological hypothesis could substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties? State the proposed intervention and why it should work, predict its speed and fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows and TOR-TILD, define composition and temperature boundaries, cite supporting evidence from prior elemental or binary results, and specify a decisive benchmark of phase free energies and derived observables that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Integrating actively learned machine-learned interatomic potentials with targeted ab initio free-energy corrections (ML-TI+FEP) can reproduce solid/liquid free energies (including vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, electron–phonon coupling) at >10× speedup versus explicit ab initio MD and 2–5× speedup versus TOR-TILD, while maintaining free-energy errors below 5 meV/atom.
generation.material_initial_state: intermetallic and multicomponent metallic alloy melts and solids near their melting point
generation.intervention: use an actively trained ML interatomic potential as a surrogate for ab initio dynamics in both phases; perform thermodynamic integration on the ML potential to obtain ΔG; then apply free‐energy perturbation corrections at a small number of key T‐P points using short ab initio MD runs
generation.conditions: compositions up to quaternary alloys; temperatures 0.8–1.2 Tm; ambient to moderate pressures (<5 GPa)
generation.structural_mediator: machine-learned interatomic potential trained on on-the-fly selected ab initio snapshots
generation.mechanism: the ML potential accurately captures the PES and anharmonic fluctuations in both phases, drastically reducing sampling cost; targeted ab initio corrections ensure systematic errors remain below threshold
generation.predicted_outcome: factor‐of‐10 reduction in wall‐clock time versus fully explicit ab initio MD; 2–5× speedup versus TOR-TILD workflows; free‐energy differences within 5 meV/atom of full ab initio results
generation.baseline: explicit ab initio MD-based free-energy evaluation (no surrogate) and TOR-TILD
generation.boundary: up to 4 elements; T/Tm between 0.8 and 1.2; P <5 GPa
generation.uncertainty: ±2 meV/atom in free-energy predictions; speedup factor may vary by ±20%

falsification_experiment.design: Apply ML-TI+FEP and full ab initio MD methods to compute melting free energies and latent heats of the Ni–Al binary and a quaternary high-entropy alloy at ambient pressure; compare results
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: ML-TI+FEP is falsified if free-energy differences exceed 10 meV/atom from explicit ab initio results or if the workflow does not achieve at least 2× speedup over TOR-TILD
